speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; to start, are you currently experiencing spinning sensations, and does head movement make it worse?

To help narrow this down quickly, is the vertigo accompanied by hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or any numbness on one side of your face?

Lastly, did this episode start while you were lying down or turning over in bed?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The episode lasting exactly three minutes while going to bed strongly suggests BPPV; are you currently symptom-free with no residual hearing loss or neurological deficits like double vision or weakness?
